DORA’S AUNTS", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u043-b0094", "target": "Я снова поклонился.", "source_sha256": "8f169cdcea57448d0c8b2f9ae9ae738fcf7290efc555243f62f4e031e6ebd0ad", "target_id": "ru-en85-u043-b0094", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "a0807ad04cf2d4a61691f50ca77366c7ac13cadb8a61a2858d41621e3b2d2b66"}, {"source_id": "en85-u043-b0095", "target": "— Мисс Тротвуд, упомянутая в письме мистера Копперфилда, — сказала мисс Кларисса, — возможно, навестит нас. Когда визиты способствуют счастью всех сторон, мы рады принимать визиты и отдавать их. Когда же для счастья всех сторон лучше, чтобы никаких визитов не было (как в случае с нашим братом Фрэнсисом и его домом), это совсем другое дело.", "source_sha256": "c7b849b9e41d201ce27c07b11def7f7a45fdbb147a5518d8e9e8fc0631443871", "target_id": "ru-en85-u043-b0095", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "883e682740fceba01d4bacfa3280316e3213fa56f2235322c45e77424a032f51"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 41, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u043-b0096", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I intimated that my aunt would be proud and delighted to make their acquaintance; though I must say I was not quite sure of their getting on very satisfactorily together. The conditions being now closed, I expressed my acknowledgements in the warmest manner; and, taking the hand, first of Miss Clarissa, and then of Miss Lavinia, pressed it, in each case, to my lips.", "sha256": "4356770807baa333613d5738e5454bbcf9acc3febbc40e5d4ecd2058c6d1b933", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[97]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0097", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Miss Lavinia then arose, and begging Mr. Traddles to excuse us for a minute, requested me to follow her. I obeyed, all in a tremble, and was conducted into another room. There I found my blessed darling stopping her ears behind the door, with her dear little face against the wall; and Jip in the plate-warmer with his head tied up in a towel.", "sha256": "0569e97e2c62db71e3da343c6a79a3b937cea0571ff56afd364698f8041a1612", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[98]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0098", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Oh! How beautiful she was in her black frock, and how she sobbed and cried at first, and wouldn’t come out from behind the door! How fond we were of one another, when she did come out at last; and what a state of bliss I was in, when we took Jip out of the plate-warmer, and restored him to the light, sneezing very much, and were all three reunited!", "sha256": "6e13a54d55440db6763864770364cf7642baa62d016240b532458cfb86bf0a0d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[99]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0099", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My dearest Dora! Now, indeed, my own for ever!’", "sha256": "7a576eb5ff7f27322a2b76802dda5a08e43c68686cc8310a0bb48329548facf5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[100]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0100", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh, DON’T!’ pleaded Dora. ‘Please!’", "sha256": "e4383520a3d6a18777b6ba3d03e2f1f651a846e2ad4788f6aeade3a3f45ae841", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[101]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0101", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Are you not my own for ever, Dora?’", "sha256": "fa3c2cefbe3cd871ad8082b26f782781ade56ede948994e3c1f7cc4a71cca1a8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[102]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0102", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh yes, of course I am!’ cried Dora, ‘but I am so frightened!’", "sha256": "e7a34d9d47a85169bdb85702d38653bcb00546a6c1d5fa6e7a4e40897bbaaa35", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[103]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0103", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Frightened, my own?’", "sha256": "ae4e6b83ee8cf5323a3874b651f845c0240d43c16c7a859f35872bac787c368d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[104]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0104", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh yes! I don’t like him,’ said Dora. ‘Why don’t he go?’", "sha256": "51c879fd1ddcd3cf33c0159624e0f1fac61e9e57fe60f40ae6e3903aa9fa5907", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[105]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0105", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Who, my life?’", "sha256": "5eeb5d4e39869428aa4951c6a975adbb5a201d9dfa26fa0dff6c1fe246ea35e3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[106]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0106", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Your friend,’ said Dora. ‘It isn’t any business of his. What a stupid he must be!’", "sha256": "20b1faec57c014c875d3af0b7c538fa58350736f00e895608da3f0a8b56b518f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[107]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0107", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My love!’ (There never was anything so coaxing as her childish ways.) ‘He is the best creature!’", "sha256": "61219d7fa6d5b6e1352dbef02cbae6e0a21a959e204777115145f02d444c9d36", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[108]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0108", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh, but we don’t want any best creatures!’ pouted Dora.", "sha256": "92732c9372174c712d1adb3044c839a46523ca944dd0de152f503b23d37d97a4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[109]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0109", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My dear,’ I argued, ‘you will soon know him well, and like him of all things. And here is my aunt coming soon; and you’ll like her of all things too, when you know her.’", "sha256": "2498e6d8eb28b2b9d86439f417d7ea2340a3c852f9ed310621763f1bd6948666", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[110]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0110", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No, please don’t bring her!’ said Dora, giving me a horrified little kiss, and folding her hands. ‘Don’t. I know she’s a naughty, mischief-making old thing! Don’t let her come here, Doady!’ which was a corruption of David.", "sha256": "0268668d2ff9d3c36d30ceb96966dcb6121eccbf342075e356997088a0124294", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[111]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0111", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Remonstrance was of no use, then; so I laughed, and admired, and was very much in love and very happy; and she showed me Jip’s new trick of standing on his hind legs in a corner—which he did for about the space of a flash of lightning, and then fell down—and I don’t know how long I should have stayed there, oblivious of Traddles, if Miss Lavinia had not come in to take me away. Miss Lavinia was very fond of Dora (she told me Dora was exactly like what she had been herself at her age—she must have altered a good deal), and she treated Dora just as if she had been a toy. I wanted to persuade Dora to come and see Traddles, but on my proposing it she ran off to her own room and locked herself in; so I went to Traddles without her, and walked away with him on air.", "sha256": "6671b61aada66c9525c02affae3b33b36111a891ed43267b485805ff0d2b62ef", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[112]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0112", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Nothing could be more satisfactory,’ said Traddles; ‘and they are very agreeable old ladies, I am sure. I shouldn’t be at all surprised if you were to be married years before me, Copperfield.’", "sha256": "3df64ce969e62ed457b2cad07d99e50de76e35dfb13516cca2f008c2a4ec5241", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[113]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0113", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Does your Sophy play on any instrument, Traddles?’ I inquired, in the pride of my heart.", "sha256": "4152d43cb542e48b868850ffac144e78df12873ba1d2ff51182d11b82a8fd320", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[114]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0114", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘She knows enough of the piano to teach it to her little sisters,’ said Traddles.", "sha256": "c99278b2bba419d4bb4ddd28739c19e965ea654202b09d7a335d480dcb86c916", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[115]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0115", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Does she sing at all?’ I asked.", "sha256": "2dbf4d7fb23f3a1355c0a6860a5b7bcfd8c22af27b069be3ec277cca234a972d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[116]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0116", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Why, she sings ballads, sometimes, to freshen up the others a little when they’re out of spirits,’ said Traddles. ‘Nothing scientific.’", "sha256": "775b8057e4f054bc8d595773bbb4bbd99d2915d0e0ea69f28df549c6a9608898", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[117]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0117", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘She doesn’t sing to the guitar?’ said I.", "sha256": "9904ddef8b5d7234d475dab95daea9a33e4182120e44828f111805e4225541d8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[118]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0118", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh dear no!’ said Traddles.", "sha256": "b55b56719e8245f7b2a0f033c7edd86397a1346784f297ef3b72258374b4c978", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[119]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0119", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Paint at all?’", "sha256": "1dc80f0482c2ae9a4cb6bd1290c5ec3e43c2f7122addd34366dc96bb5c49b90e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[120]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0120", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Not at all,’ said Traddles.", "sha256": "324b572c9d125e4aff153253990f096f77109f4784f4d62e86b8d48d1a25e806", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[121]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0121", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I promised Traddles that he should hear Dora sing, and see some of her flower-painting. He said he should like it very much, and we went home arm in arm in great good humour and delight. I encouraged him to talk about Sophy, on the way; which he did with a loving reliance on her that I very much admired. I compared her in my mind with Dora, with considerable inward satisfaction; but I candidly admitted to myself that she seemed to be an excellent kind of girl for Traddles, too.", "sha256": "b4703c12ba843067ee6615b7167609a7c613a1f5a6cde9ff3ca01a6500a90403", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[122]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0122", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Of course my aunt was immediately made acquainted with the successful issue of the conference, and with all that had been said and done in the course of it. She was happy to see me so happy, and promised to call on Dora’s aunts without loss of time. But she took such a long walk up and down our rooms that night, while I was writing to Agnes, that I began to think she meant to walk till morning.", "sha256": "f939078162c85e2a4a5f5c17c5abc249491f26df6ec0d95e3769df78248bda80", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[123]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0123", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My letter to Agnes was a fervent and grateful one, narrating all the good effects that had resulted from my following her advice. She wrote, by return of post, to me. Her letter was hopeful, earnest, and cheerful. She was always cheerful from that time.", "sha256": "3f530bcc0be9f0c5a6d8e31134c6d41de8bdfddebe80b1e2b79b278ee25a6881", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[124]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0124", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I had my hands more full than ever, now. My daily journeys to Highgate considered, Putney was a long way off; and I naturally wanted to go there as often as I could. The proposed tea-drinkings being quite impracticable, I compounded with Miss Lavinia for permission to visit every Saturday afternoon, without detriment to my privileged Sundays. So, the close of every week was a delicious time for me; and I got through the rest of the week by looking forward to it.", "sha256": "ddc7f415bd1b749f066988b961a696789879433d7b31f74bb65bbc5652cb1331", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[125]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0125", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I was wonderfully relieved to find that my aunt and Dora’s aunts rubbed on, all things considered, much more smoothly than I could have expected. My aunt made her promised visit within a few days of the conference; and within a few more days, Dora’s aunts called upon her, in due state and form. Similar but more friendly exchanges took place afterwards, usually at intervals of three or four weeks. I know that my aunt distressed Dora’s aunts very much, by utterly setting at naught the dignity of fly-conveyance, and walking out to Putney at extraordinary times, as shortly after breakfast or just before tea; likewise by wearing her bonnet in any manner that happened to be comfortable to her head, without at all deferring to the prejudices of civilization on that subject. But Dora’s aunts soon agreed to regard my aunt as an eccentric and somewhat masculine lady, with a strong understanding; and although my aunt occasionally ruffled the feathers of Dora’s aunts, by expressing heretical opinions on various points of ceremony, she loved me too well not to sacrifice some of her little peculiarities to the general harmony.", "sha256": "cd836070a7b0bb8f5aa82dfb4ee40d282e24f41571577db514f6e81dcfffaa2f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[126]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0126", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The only member of our small society who positively refused to adapt himself to circumstances, was Jip. He never saw my aunt without immediately displaying every tooth in his head, retiring under a chair, and growling incessantly: with now and then a doleful howl, as if she really were too much for his feelings. All kinds of treatment were tried with him, coaxing, scolding, slapping, bringing him to Buckingham Street (where he instantly dashed at the two cats, to the terror of all beholders); but he never could prevail upon himself to bear my aunt’s society. He would sometimes think he had got the better of his objection, and be amiable for a few minutes; and then would put up his snub nose, and howl to that extent, that there was nothing for it but to blind him and put him in the plate-warmer. At length, Dora regularly muffled him in a towel and shut him up there, whenever my aunt was reported at the door.", "sha256": "7b713da21342dd90e9e7d86003cac71e2ac851b3fa163356f231aadec03c5cec", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[127]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0127", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "One thing troubled me much, after we had fallen into this quiet train. It was, that Dora seemed by one consent to be regarded like a pretty toy or plaything. My aunt, with whom she gradually became familiar, always called her Little Blossom; and the pleasure of Miss Lavinia’s life was to wait upon her, curl her hair, make ornaments for her, and treat her like a pet child. What Miss Lavinia did, her sister did as a matter of course. It was very odd to me; but they all seemed to treat Dora, in her degree, much as Dora treated Jip in his.", "sha256": "0ba8645f8c86e741ec54945431a20a7098114df8cf0b3bfc9d9b16350aeca381", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[128]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
